akhfash:13-13.t: He said ﴿أَنْ أَقِيمُواْ ٱلدِّينَ وَلاَ [تَتَفَرَّقُواْ فِيهِ]﴾ as an explanation, as though He said "it is: establish the religion", as a badal (substitute).

akhfash:15-15.t: And He said ﴿وَأُمِرْتُ لأَعْدِلَ بَيْنَكُمُ﴾, i.e. I was commanded so that I would be just.

akhfash:23-23.t:
And He said ﴿إِلاَّ ٱلْمَوَدَّةَ فِي ٱلْقُرْبَىٰ﴾: an exception falling outside (the first part). He means — and Allah knows best — "except that I mention the love of my kinship".
As for ﴿يُبَشِّرُ﴾, you say "بَشَّرْتُه" and "أبشَرْتُه" (I gave him good tidings) [and] some said "أَبْشُرُهُ" (light), which is from "بَشَرْتُ"; it occurs in poetry. The poet said [in the basīṭ metre; this is poetic witness no. 266]:
وَقَدْ أَرُوحُ إِلَى الحانوتِ أَبْشُرُهُ * بالرَّحْلِ فَوْقَ ذُرَى العَيْرانَةِ الأُجُد
(Many an evening I go to the wine-shop, gladdening it (with my coming), with my saddle on the hump of a strong, sturdy she-camel.)
Abū al-Ḥasan (al-Akhfash) said: "Yūnus recited this verse to me thus." And He made ﴿ٱلَّذِي يُبَشِّرُ﴾ a noun for the act, as though it were "التَبْشِير" (the giving of good tidings), as He said ﴿فَٱصْدَعْ بِمَا تُؤْمَرُ﴾, i.e. proclaim the command. It cannot be that you imply the bāʾ in it and omit it, because you do not say "كَلِّمْ الذِي مَرَرْتُ" (speak to the one I passed) while meaning "by him".

akhfash:26-26.t: And His word ﴿وَيَسْتَجِيبُ ٱلَّذِينَ آمَنُواْ﴾, i.e. "responded"; He made them the agents.

akhfash:43-43.t: And He said ﴿وَلَمَن صَبَرَ وَغَفَرَ إِنَّ ذَلِكَ لَمِنْ عَزْمِ ٱلأُمُورِ﴾: as for the lām in ﴿وَلَمَن صَبَرَ﴾, it is the lām of the mubtadaʾ. As for "that", its meaning — and Allah knows best — is "that, on his part, is among the resolute matters". You may say: "مَرَرْتُ بدارٍ الذراعُ بِدِرْهَمٍ" (I passed by a house, the cubit at a dirham), i.e. "the cubit of it at a dirham", and "مررت بِبُرٍّ قفيزٌ بدرهم" (I passed by wheat, a qafīz at a dirham), i.e. "a qafīz of it". As for beginning with "إنّ" in this position, it is like ﴿قُلْ إِنَّ ٱلْمَوْتَ ٱلَّذِي تَفِرُّونَ مِنْهُ فَإِنَّهُ مُلاَقِيكُمْ﴾; beginning with the like of this is allowed when the speech is long, in such a position.

akhfash:45-45.t: And He said ﴿يَنظُرُونَ مِن طَرْفٍ خَفِيٍّ﴾: He made "الطَرْفَ" the eye, as though He said "and their looking is from a weak eye" — and Allah knows best. Yūnus said: "﴿مِن طَرْفٍ﴾ is like 'بِطَرْفٍ' (with a glance), as the Arabs say: 'ضربتُه في السَّيْف' and 'بِالسَّيْفِ' (I struck him with the sword)."

akhfash:53-53.t: And He said ﴿أَلاَ إِلَى ٱللَّهِ تَصِيرُ ٱلأُمُورُ﴾ because Allah, Blessed and Exalted, takes charge of things without His creation on the Day of Resurrection, whereas in this world He has assigned some matters to them — to jurists, rulers and the like.
